newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products - Gulf Coast gasoline ticks up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products - Gulf Coast gasoline ticks up.

text.p: Cash differentials on U.S. Gulf Coast gasoline ticked up a tad on Friday, but most traders insisted the move was nothing to write home about.
In fact, action across the board in spot markets east of the Rocky Mountains was rather subdued ahead of the weekend.

Underlying NYMEX futures meanwhile, led by gasoline, settled lower Friday on growing views that gasoline inventories are looking bearishly ample. The July crude contract expired Friday 12 cents lower at $18.55 a barrel.
U.S. GULF

Some traders said strength in Gulf gasoline started with "M2" northern grade regular conventional gasoline, which had a Colonial Pipeline scheduling deadline Friday. Prompt M2 was talked as high as 3.20 cents under July NYMEX.
The M2 strength spread to the M1 southern grade regular conventional, which got done at levels about 0.40 cent firmer of 3.10 under the July print.

But some players, noting high refinery runs rates are innundating the Houston markets with product, downplayed the firmer differentials, saying liquidity was poor enough for small deals to affect the market too easily.
Also, low sulphur 74-grade diesel was heard, but not confirmed, done at 1.80 cents under July NYMEX -- a touch weaker than on Thursday.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Activity in New York Harbor remained subdued Friday, with few market players actively seeking barrels.
"Everything in the Harbor is pretty well offered. We're looking for bidders," one East Coast trader said.
Prompt regular conventional M2 northern grade gasoline changed hands at 3.00 cents under the July NYMEX, the lower end of the range seen Thurday, according to the trader.
Coventional 93-octane D2 gasoline was talked near 4.50 cents over the July NYMEX, while the premium reformulated V2 gasoline was seen near 7.50 cents over the NYMEX.
Market watchers said the regular reformulated A2 gasoline was offered near 0.35 cent under the July NYMEX, though no confirmed deals were noted.
MIDCONTINENT

Midcontinent products showed little price movement in early Friday action, traders said, though Group Three gasoline appeared to be holding gains made Thurdays from refinery buying interest, traders said.

Differentials for the prompt regular gasoline held steady with late Thursday levels, between 5.00 and 5.25 cents over the July NYMEX, while end of the month barrels were talked between 4.25 and 4.50 cents over the NYMEX.
Traders attributed Thursday's gains to the continued delays on the Houston-to-Tulsa-to-Chicago Explorer Pipeline, which prompted some refiners to short cover on prompt commitments.
Market watchers said distillate activity remained very thin early Friday, with few players evident in the Chicago arena.
-- New York Oil Desk +1 212 859 1620
